mainTopic: Closing the debate about backing out of a decision (רב יוסף vs. רבה), then the משנה's rule that a woman passes her estate to her son and husband, and the source that a mother inherits from her son
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier debate about how long someone can back out of a decision. רב יוסף says it is too late once the parties move to a new topic, and רבה says it is too late once they stand up. רבה explains רב יהודה's case as one where the people stood up and sat down again, so the case proves nothing. Even so, the גמרא rules like רב יוסף in three topics: a field, the same topic, and half. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks why 'a woman to her son' needs to be taught, since a man inheriting his mother was already stated. The answer is that the son is compared to the husband: neither one who died first can pass the woman's estate on 'from the grave.' Finally, רבי יוחנן brings a תורה source from the word 'מטות' (tribes) that a mother inherits from her son, just as a father does.

steps.title: רבה explains רב יהודה's case as people who stood up and sat down again
steps.stepSummary: Finishing an earlier back-and-forth, the גמרא says רב יהודה's ruling can be read according to רבה as a case where the parties stood up and then sat back down, so it is no proof for רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...from one topic to another topic. So too here, it is a case where they stood up and then sat back down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a discussion from the previous section. It deflects a proof by saying רב יהודה's case was one where the people got up and sat down again, which ends the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was how long someone can still back out of a decision. רב יוסף says it is too late once the parties switch to a new topic, while רבה says it is too late only once they stand up. Since רב יהודה's case can be read as people who stood up and sat down again, רבה can explain it too, so it does not prove רב יוסף's view.

keyTerms.meaning: from one topic to another topic
so too here; the same applies here
they stood up and then sat back down

phrases.english: from one topic to another topic;
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous section: once they switch to a new topic, it is too late to back out.

phrases.english: so too here,
it is a case where they stood up and then sat back down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a defense that started before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling looked like it supported רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה was talking about people who stood up and sat down again, which fits רבה's view too.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב יוסף in three topics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב יוסף on dividing a field, on backing out while still on the same topic, and on giving away half of one's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב יוסף in the case of a field, the same topic, and half.
steps.whatsHappening: Even though the proof for רב יוסף was pushed away, the גמרא gives a final ruling in his favor in three separate topics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof can be rejected and the ruling can still follow that view. Here the גמרא lists three places where רב יוסף's view is the הלכה. The three short words each point to a different סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: and the הלכה follows his view
a field (the case of dividing a field)
topic (backing out while still on the same topic)
half (the case of half one's property)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רב יוסף in three topics: dividing a field, backing out while still on the same topic, and half of one's property.
steps.confusionAlert: Rejecting a proof does not mean the view was rejected. The proof failed, but the ruling still goes like רב יוסף.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows רב יוסף
in the field, the same topic, and half.
phrases.notes: These are three short memory hooks for three סוגיות: dividing a field (דף יב), the backing-out question here, and half one's property (דף קמג).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling after the proof was deflected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The halacha is like רב יוסף in three topics: a field, the same topic, and half.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say a woman passes her estate to her son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'a woman to her son' and asks why it is needed, since the first clause already taught that a man inherits his mother and his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A woman to her son,' and so on. Why do I need this as well? The first clause already taught: a man inherits his mother, and a man inherits his wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It challenges the line as repeating what the משנה already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause said a son inherits his mother and a husband inherits his wife. The later clause, 'a woman passes her estate to her son,' seems to say the same thing from the woman's side. The גמרא assumes the משנה does not repeat itself for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this as well?
the first clause of the משנה
and so on; the quote continues

phrases.english: 'A woman to her son,' and so on.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: a woman passes her estate to her son and husband, but does not inherit from them.

phrases.english: Why do I need this as well?
It was already taught in the first clause:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִישׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ, וְהָאִישׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ!
phrases.english: 'A man inherits his mother, and a man inherits his wife!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause 'a woman to her son'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: the first clause already taught that a son inherits his mother.

steps.title: The son is like the husband: no inheriting from the grave
steps.stepSummary: The extra clause teaches that a son is compared to a husband. Just as a husband who died first cannot pass his wife's estate on, a son who died first cannot pass his mother's estate to his brothers from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that 'a woman to her son' is like 'a woman to her husband.' Just as with a woman and her husband, the husband does not inherit his wife from the grave, so too with a woman and her son, the son does not inherit his mother from the grave in order to pass it on to his brothers from his father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the clause is not a repeat. It is placed next to 'a woman to her husband' to teach that the two follow the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband dies before his wife, his own heirs do not get her estate through him; her own relatives inherit it. The משנה puts the son in the same line to teach the same rule for him. If the son dies before his mother, his brothers from a different mother cannot claim her estate through him.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it teaches us
similar to; like
in the grave; after he has already died
to pass on an inheritance
brothers from the same father (but not the same mother)

steps.whatToRemember: A son who dies before his mother is like a husband who dies before his wife. He cannot pass her estate on 'from the grave,' so his brothers from his father do not get it. Her own relatives inherit.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Inheriting in the grave' does not mean the dead person owns anything. It means: can his heirs claim the estate through him because he would have inherited it if he were alive? Here the answer is no.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for who gets a woman's property when her son or husband died before her.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that a woman to her son
is like a woman to her husband;
just as with a woman and her husband,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבַּעַל יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר,
phrases.english: the husband does not inherit his wife from the grave,
phrases.notes: He means a husband who died before his wife. His own heirs can't claim her estate through him.

phrases.english: so too with a woman and her son,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַבֵּן יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִמּוֹ בַּקֶּבֶר,
phrases.english: the son does not inherit his mother from the grave,
to pass it on to his brothers from his father.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison drawn from where the clause is placed in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause just repeats that a son inherits his mother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause compares son to husband: neither inherits from the grave.

steps.title: A mother inherits from her son, learned from 'מטות'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יהודה בן רבי שמעון, says that by תורה law a father inherits from his son and a mother does too. He learns it from the plural word 'מטות' (tribes), which compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יהודה בן רבי שמעון: By תורה law, a father inherits his son, and a woman inherits her son, as it says 'tribes.' The verse compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe: just as in the father's tribe a father inherits his son, so too in the mother's tribe a woman inherits her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement giving the תורה source that a mother inherits from her son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the plural 'מטות,' meaning more than one tribe: the father's tribe and the mother's tribe. Putting them together in one word is a היקש, a comparison that gives them the same rule. Since a father inherits his son, a mother does too.

keyTerms.meaning: by תורה law
tribes (plural)
compares; links two things so they share a rule (היקש)
the mother's tribe
the father's tribe

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a mother inheriting from her son is a תורה law, not only a rabbinic rule.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יהודה בן רבי שמעון:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה – הָאָב יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: By תורה law, a father inherits his son,
and a woman inherits her son;
as it says: 'tribes.'
It compares the mother's tribe to the father's tribe:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַטֵּה הָאָב – אָב יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ,
phrases.english: just as in the father's tribe a father inherits his son,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַטֵּה הָאֵם – אִשָּׁה יוֹרֶשֶׁת אֶת בְּנָהּ.
phrases.english: so too in the mother's tribe a woman inherits her son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new related teaching about a mother inheriting her son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By תורה law both a father and a mother inherit from their son, learned from the comparison in the word 'מטות.'
